author: Lucy Quaggin
description:
As Chinese leader Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump wrapped up their three-day state visit on Friday, a stark contrast in the two presidential couples’ hand-holding dynamics was on display, body language experts said.
The exchanges between Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, and Trump and first lady Melania Trump, were closely followed on the trip, with the couples’ activities together on Friday culminating in an outing at the National Archives Museum in Washington.
The couples’ divergent...
title: What Donald Trump and Xi Jinping revealed in the body language with their wives

author: Alex Lo
description:
Washington and Beijing have spent nearly a decade trading tariffs, export controls and blacklists, with each round threatening rupture. Yet they keep recovering from the brink.
Tensions soared before summits and plunged immediately after. For example, in 2019 at Osaka, Trump walked back threats to impose tariffs on US$300 billion of Chinese goods and eased curbs on Huawei after Beijing reportedly agreed to buy American farm goods. In Busan last October, he lowered tariffs and shelved export...
title: China and the US can make nice, if not peace

author: Nayan Seth
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has completed a whirlwind 43-hour trip to the United States, his first state visit to the country in more than a decade, with US President Donald Trump pulling out all the stops to make it a grand affair.
The two leaders met several times during the visit, including at a ceremonial airport welcome, the White House reception and bilateral talks on a wide range of topics including trade, tariffs and Taiwan.
They also attended a state dinner in Xi’s honour with top...
title: Trade deliverables, Taiwan push and ‘strategic stability’: key Xi-Trump takeaways overall

author: Igor Patrick
description:
China is poised to decide which of two Latin American women becomes the first to lead the United Nations, after three rounds of informal voting in the Security Council failed to produce a favourite.
Several UN delegations that spoke to the South China Morning Post over the past three days said Beijing was weighing Rebeca Grynspan, the Costa Rican economist who heads UN Trade and Development, and Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett, Guyana’s ambassador to the UN.
The same delegations said China had ruled...
title: China set to decide if Costa Rican or Guyanese diplomat becomes first woman UN chief

author: Orange Wang,Caroline Lin
description:
Domestic US political turmoil and Donald Trump’s feud with the media overshadowed a summit that Beijing hoped would project an image of China on equal footing and help stabilise ties with the United States.
Trump rolled out the full red-carpet treatment for Chinese President Xi Jinping as he paid his first state visit to the US in over a decade.
In addition to Trump and his wife Melania greeting Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan on the tarmac on arrival, the “many special arrangements” included a...
title: What summit? US TV blackout and midterms turmoil overshadow red-carpet treatment

author: Simon Tay
description:
The good news is, when US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping met in Washington this week, neither chose confrontation. Amid the high pomp and ceremony, what China has called “constructive strategic stability” continues.
Even an uneasy truce in great power relations can be useful. Both recognise the considerable incentive to prevent their economic rivalry from spiralling out of control. Even limited understandings can reduce risks in artificial intelligence (AI) and other...
title: In a US-China world, Asean must do more than avoid choosing sides

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
Throughout President Xi Jinping’s state visit to Washington, Chinese aesthetics were not confined to first lady Peng Liyuan, long an ambassador of Chinese fashion, but also appeared in the outfits of other senior Chinese officials and even members of the US delegation.
At the state dinner in the White House on Thursday, Xi and other senior Chinese officials – including his chief of staff Cai Qi and foreign minister Wang Yi – wore black Mao suits.
Notably, while Xi has regularly worn the attire...
title: Chinese aesthetics abound at Washington summit, from Mao suits to peony trousers

description:

If the American guests seated at the head table with President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump at Thursday’s White House state dinner were any indication, Washington now views its relationship with Beijing largely through the prism of technology.
2....

author: Nayan Seth,Lucy Quaggin,Josephine Ma
description:
In a surprise nod to shared history, US President Donald Trump called China a World War II ally as he welcomed Xi Jinping to the White House on Thursday ahead of summit talks.
But the historical reference was far from one-sided, with both leaders repeatedly referring to the joint fight against Japanese aggression as they sought to emphasise the long history of US-China friendship and the need to seek common ground.
“If we focus on our common interests, I’m confident there is much we can...
title: Trump hails WWII ‘ally’ China as Xi tells of bonds ‘forged in blood and fire’

author: Amber Wang
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping pressed his US counterpart Donald Trump to explicitly oppose Taiwan independence – a call that would require a shift in Washington’s long-standing position and further restraint on American arms sales to the island, according to analysts.
During the meeting between the two leaders on Thursday, Xi said he hoped the US side would “adhere to the correct position of opposing ‘Taiwan independence’”, according to a statement from the foreign ministry in Beijing.
The...
title: Xi presses Trump to take the next step on Taiwan: oppose independence

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Taiwanese officials and observers have reacted cautiously to the Washington summit between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, with uncertainty lingering over what the two leaders discussed about the island.
The only public mention of Taiwan after Thursday’s closed-door talks between the pair came from Beijing’s official statement, which said Xi had urged Trump to “oppose ‘Taiwan independence’” and “handle the Taiwan question with caution”. The White House did not immediately give its own detailed...
title: Trump’s warm welcome for Xi met with caution and uncertainty in Taiwan

author: Caroline Lin
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has not only made history as the first Chinese leader to undertake two formal state visits to the United States, he is also the only Chinese leader to be spending two Mid-Autumn Festivals on American soil.
Xi offered festive greetings during his toast at Thursday’s state banquet.
“As I speak, my compatriots in China are celebrating Mid-Autumn Festival – a cherished occasion for family reunions according to Chinese tradition. I wish you all a very happy Mid-Autumn...
title: Xi Jinping marks second Mid-Autumn Festival in US during state visit

author: William Zheng
description:
Amid the polished silverware and fine crystal stemware on display at the state dinner in the White House on Thursday sat the vacuum flasks brought by Chinese President Xi Jinping and first lady Peng Liyuan.
The couple’s flasks, black for Xi and white for Peng, were spotted on their table during the formal dinner, signalling a subtle self-assurance as cultural authenticity met high diplomacy.
Extending this everyday practice to the White House banquet was in tune with the host nation’s own...
title: Why did Xi and China’s first lady bring their own flasks to White House banquet?

author: Liu Zhen
description:
Chinese viewers watching Donald Trump welcome Xi Jinping to the White House on Thursday may have been puzzled by the US president’s reference to the “Chinese phrase” gung-ho. Turning to Baidu – or increasingly, Doubao, the country’s most popular AI chatbot – they may well have asked: what Chinese expression is he referring to?
It sounds Chinese, but gung-ho is neither part of everyday usage nor an idiom drawn from classical texts – making this moment almost as baffling as when US Secretary of...
title: The Chinese roots of ‘gung-ho’ as Trump and Xi look to shared history

author: Raymond Ma,Neil Denslow
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump discussed artificial intelligence (AI) and Taiwan at the White House on Thursday as part of a state visit dominated by pageantry.
On AI, Xi said that “the right thing to do is to draw on each other’s strengths, not guard against each other”, according to a statement from the Chinese foreign ministry. He also backed continued dialogue about risks, joint efforts to prevent misuse and keeping AI under human control.
Trump earlier said on...
title: Xi at White House, trade-war truce extension, Golden Week travel

author: Laura Zhou
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping’s trip to the US will conclude not at the diplomatic negotiating table, but in front of America’s founding documents.
After morning tea in the White House Red Room, US President Donald Trump and his wife Melania will take Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan on a tour of the National Archives, the home of the Declaration of Independence, the Constitution and other texts that established the basis of the US government.
According to the Office of the First Lady, the two couples...
title: Why is the National Archives the last stop on Xi and Trump’s summit itinerary?

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
Property developer-turned-president Donald Trump appeared to relish showing off the White House’s latest building works to Xi Jinping on Thursday, eager to give his Chinese counterpart a glimpse of his construction ambitions since they last met in China.
In May, Trump was hosted at Beijing’s Great Hall of the People, a sprawling complex that the US president compares with his planned White House ballroom.
After their talks in the Oval Office, Trump led Xi out to the South Lawn, where his...
title: Trump gives Xi a tour of his pet White House building projects, including the ballroom

author: William Zheng
description:
Zhou Hongxu, the official who oversees President Xi Jinping’s security, made an appearance at the White House state banquet on Thursday night, alongside a cohort of other rising Chinese officials.
The banquet’s guest list described the 55-year-old People’s Liberation Army (PLA) major general as both director of the Central Guard Bureau and deputy director of the Communist Party’s General Office – the ruling party’s powerful administrative nerve centre.
Earlier this month, Zhou joined Xi for a...
title: Xi’s security chief among cohort of rising officials at White House banquet

author: Carol Yang
description:
When US President Donald Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping in the East Room, every detail of the state dinner was steeped in symbolism, with sparkling wine served as a nod to a pivotal moment in Sino-US relations and references to “ping-pong diplomacy”.
The meal opened with a toast of Schramsberg Blanc de Noirs, a vineyard selected to honour the historic 1972 “Toast to Peace” shared by then US president Richard Nixon and Chinese premier Zhou Enlai, according to the first lady’s...
title: From wine to ping-pong, Trump and Xi’s state dinner is heavy on historic symbolism

author: Caroline Lin
description:
While their husbands held talks at the White House, Melania Trump hosted Peng Liyuan at the Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art on Thursday, where the famed Chinese soprano softly hummed along to a youth choir’s performance of a familiar classic.
Footage shows the Hope Chinese School youth choir waving Chinese and American national flags during their rendition of the song “Jasmine Flower”, while Peng watches with a smile, her lips moving along to the lyrics.


As the performance ends, she...
title: Pitch perfect cultural diplomacy wins heart of China’s first lady Peng Liyuan

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping broke into rare laughter as his US counterpart Donald Trump showed him a framed “autopen” displayed in place of the former American leader Joe Biden’s portrait during a White House tour.
The viral moment stood out against the Chinese leader’s otherwise restrained demeanour during his first state visit to the United States in more than a decade.
A video released by the White House on social media showed Trump taking Xi along the White House colonnade on Thursday...
title: China’s Xi shares a rare laugh on White House tour at Trump’s Biden autopen joke

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
The US president’s eldest daughter Ivanka Trump had a front-row seat at a White House welcome ceremony for President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan on Thursday, wearing a dress by Chinese fashion designer Guo Pei.
Trump, in a robin’s egg blue dress and matching jacket, and her 15-year-old daughter Arabella Kushner occupied a prominent position at the ceremony, alongside Vice-President J.D. Vance and his wife, Usha Vance.
The arrangement drew attention since members of Donald Trump’s cabinet...
title: Ivanka Trump takes front-row seat to welcome Xi in dress by Chinese designer Guo Pei

author: Zhang Tong
description:
Chinese researchers have showed a handheld quantum magnetometer built for hunting submarines in a striking real-world test: it tracked a subway train rumbling beneath a city street.
The device, developed by Peng Xinhua and colleagues at the University of Science and Technology of China, is described in a study published on September 14 in Acta Physica Sinica.
Though it is scarcely larger than a pencil and draws only 5 watts of power, it can isolate the magnetic disturbance caused by a moving...
title: China tested a handheld submarine detector. It tracked a subway train underground

author: Orange Wang
description:
Before setting off for Washington on Wednesday, Chinese President Xi Jinping had some correspondence to attend to.
Dozens of students from 10 US universities, including Harvard, had written to Xi about their experiences on an exchange trip to China this year.
According to the State Council, Xi responded with a call to the students to advance cooperation between the two countries.
The gesture extended a pattern.
For decades, Beijing has often turned to unofficial channels, from prominent...
title: From ping-pong to pickleball: China’s unofficial approach to diplomatic messaging

author: Dewey Sim,Ji Siqi,Holly Chik
description:
Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump addressed top American business executives and officials in the White House’s East Room on Thursday evening, ahead of a state dinner.
The dinner capped a tightly scheduled day for the two leaders, who delivered speeches in the morning hailing close ties and urging deeper cooperation.
During the day, Xi and Trump held their second face-to-face meeting this year – which Trump called a “great meeting” – touching on issues including Taiwan, the Middle East...
title: How was dinner? Takeaways from Xi and Trump’s evening at the White House

author: Holly Chik
description:
As Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet at the White House for a state dinner on Thursday, culinary diplomacy is on the menu for guests who include business leaders and government officials.
“The menu showcases American ingredients with subtle Chinese influence, bringing the culinary traditions of both nations together,” the office of American first lady Melania Trump said.
Xi is dressed in a black Zhongshan suit – colloquially known as a “Mao suit” – while Chinese first lady Peng Liyuan is wearing...
title: Culinary diplomacy on the menu for Xi and Trump at the White House
